Appendix F
MAMMAL HABITAT AND FOOD REQUIREMENT ON THE WESTMORELAND RESOURCE LEASE
The listing gives habitat and food requirements of mammals that occur or may occur on the Westmoreland Resources lease where family groups are similar in requirements the family will be treated as a group, otherwise individual species requirements are listed.
Name: Shews - Family Soricidae
Habitat: Moist areas - Forests, brushlands, open country (Masked).
Arid areas - Sagebrush, bunchgrass (merrians).
Foods: Earthworms, insects, snails, spiders, mice.
Name: Plainnose Bats - Vespertilionidae
Habitat: Nocturnal, free roaming in search of food. Occur
in caves, tunnels, buildings, forests.
Foods: Insectivorous.
Name: Raccoon - Procyon lotor
Habitat: Dense or rocky areas near water.
Foods: Omniviorous. Frogs, crayfish, insects, fish, small
mammals, alfalfa, corn, barley.
Miscellaneous: May damage crops and poultry. Fur of value.
Edible.
Name: Shorttail Weasel (Ermine) - Mustela erminea
Habitat: Areas of dense vegetation growth, near water.
Mostly nocturnal.
Foods: Rabbits, rodents, snakes, frogs, fish, birds, eggs.
Miscellaneous: Winter pelts are of value. Good mousers.
Name: Longtail Weasel - Mustela frenata
Habitat: All areas near water. Mostly nocturnal.
Foods: Rabbits, rodents, snakes, frogs, fish, birds, eggs.
Miscellaneous: Winter pelts are of value. Kills many
rodents.
Name: Mink - Mustela vison
Habitat: Aquatic. Found near lakes, marshes, streams.
Foods: Rodents, snakes, crustaceans, frogs, birds, eggs.
Miscellaneous: Valuable for their pelts.
Name: Badger - Taxidea taxus
Habitat: Open areas of grasslands and deserts. Mostly
noctural.
Foods: Rodents, rabbits, insects, grouse, lizards.
